title: Classify triangles by angles: right, acute, obtuse

lesson.title: Naming Triangles by Their Angles

steps.say: You already know how to spot an acute angle, a right angle, and an obtuse angle. Today we use that skill on triangles, so you can look at any triangle and give it the right name.

visual.caption: A right angle — you already know this one

steps.say: Here is the trick. A triangle always has three angles, so you check all three and look for the biggest one. If the biggest angle is exactly ninety degrees, it is a right triangle. If the biggest angle is smaller than ninety degrees, then all three are small and it is an acute triangle. If the biggest angle is bigger than ninety degrees, it is an obtuse triangle.

visual.caption: Three angles — find the biggest one

steps.say: Let's try a real one. Ms. Yuanyuan cut a corner off a piece of cardboard for the school garden sign. The three angles measured seventy degrees, sixty degrees, and fifty degrees. The biggest angle is seventy degrees, and seventy is less than ninety, so every angle is small. That makes it an acute triangle.

visual.caption: The biggest angle is only 70° — acute triangle

steps.say: Now the second one. A triangle piece of pizza had angles of one hundred ten degrees, forty degrees, and thirty degrees. One hundred ten is bigger than ninety, so that one wide angle is enough. Even though the other two are small, we call the whole triangle obtuse.

visual.caption: One angle wider than 90° makes it obtuse

steps.say: Here is the mistake lots of kids make. When a right triangle is turned upside down or tipped on its side, they say it is not a right triangle any more. But turning a shape never changes its angles. If you tape a right triangle to a spinning ferry wheel, that ninety degree corner is still exactly ninety degrees. So spin it, flip it, tip it — a right triangle stays a right triangle.

visual.caption: Turned around, but still the same three angles

steps.say: So remember, find the biggest angle in the triangle, and that one angle tells you the name.

lesson.answer: Look at the biggest angle: exactly 90° is right, under 90° is acute, over 90° is obtuse — and turning the triangle never changes it.

practice.question: Draw a triangle on paper for a road sign in Vancouver. Its three angles are one hundred degrees, forty five degrees, and thirty five degrees. What kind of triangle is it by its angles? And if you turn your paper upside down, does the answer change?
practice.answer: It is an obtuse triangle, because the biggest angle, one hundred degrees, is bigger than ninety degrees. Turning the paper upside down does not change anything — it is still an obtuse triangle.
